instruction:
Required four-software transfer workflow: LibreCAD -> FreeCAD -> KiCad -> Blender. Start from the provided seed DXF /home/user/Desktop/seed_round_gauge_bezel.dxf; do not start from a blank or unrelated drawing. This is a chained workflow: every later stage must read an artifact from the previous stage, and every required intermediate file must be saved on the Desktop. The design token for this task is EW4G04; keep this token visible in the DXF labels and KiCad silkscreen. The Blender output must visibly consume the stage-2 STL and stage-3 SVG through Blender's native import/export operations.

Design goal: Round instrument gauge bezel with OLED and encoder board. This case is intentionally different from the other benchmark cases: domain=instrument_display_bezel, mechanical target=an instrument front view with smoky display lens and a raised encoder knob, electronics target=a circular gauge PCB carrying an OLED display, encoder, buzzer, mode button, and I2C header.

1. LibreCAD stage: open the provided seed file /home/user/Desktop/seed_round_gauge_bezel.dxf in LibreCAD, use it as the starting drawing, complete the required 2D geometry, remove all GUIDE construction entities, and save /home/user/Desktop/stage1_round_gauge_bezel.dxf. Use millimeters. Use layers OUTLINE, WINDOW, HOLE, LABEL. The overall drawing envelope must be 118 mm x 118 mm. Include the required circular features: center (59,59) radius 59; center (59,59) radius 34; center (59,12) radius 2.1; center (106,59) radius 2.1; center (59,106) radius 2.1; center (12,59) radius 2.1. Add readable labels EW4G04, OLED, ENCODER, BEZEL on the LABEL layer.
2. FreeCAD stage: import /home/user/Desktop/stage1_round_gauge_bezel.dxf in FreeCAD. Create the 3D mechanical body from that LibreCAD DXF, and export the body as /home/user/Desktop/stage2_round_gauge_bezel.stl with an approximate bounding size of 118 mm x 118 mm x 18 mm. Then, from the same FreeCAD model, export a top-face or board-interface outline for KiCad as /home/user/Desktop/stage2_round_gauge_bezel_handoff_outline.dxf. This handoff DXF must represent the same XY envelope as the FreeCAD body and include the visible labels FREECAD_TO_KICAD and EW4G04.
3. KiCad stage: open KiCad, create a PCB from /home/user/Desktop/stage2_round_gauge_bezel_handoff_outline.dxf by importing the handoff DXF as the Edge.Cuts board outline, and save the KiCad board as /home/user/Desktop/stage3_round_gauge_bezel_board.kicad_pcb. Add F.SilkS silkscreen text carrying KICAD_TO_BLENDER, EDGE_FROM_STAGE2_HANDOFF, the stage2 handoff filename, EW4G04, and these board tokens: EW4G04, OLED-DS1, ENCODER-SW1, BUZZER-BZ1, BTN-MODE, I2C-J1. Then use KiCad's plot/export workflow to create the Blender handoff SVG /home/user/Desktop/stage3_round_gauge_bezel_board_profile.svg from the same Edge.Cuts outline.
4. Blender stage: open Blender. Import /home/user/Desktop/stage2_round_gauge_bezel.stl with File > Import > STL, then import /home/user/Desktop/stage3_round_gauge_bezel_board_profile.svg with File > Import > Scalable Vector Graphics (.svg). Keep the imported STL body object and the imported SVG board/profile curves in the scene so the exported GLB carries Blender import evidence such as stage2_round_gauge_bezel and stage3_round_gauge_bezel_board_profile.svg. You may leave Blender's default cube/camera/light or remove them; do not manually inject handoff metadata. Export glTF Binary (.glb) as /home/user/Desktop/stage4_round_gauge_bezel.glb.

Required deliverables on the Desktop: /home/user/Desktop/stage1_round_gauge_bezel.dxf, /home/user/Desktop/stage2_round_gauge_bezel.stl, /home/user/Desktop/stage2_round_gauge_bezel_handoff_outline.dxf, /home/user/Desktop/stage3_round_gauge_bezel_board.kicad_pcb, /home/user/Desktop/stage3_round_gauge_bezel_board_profile.svg, /home/user/Desktop/stage4_round_gauge_bezel.glb.

[Software] Use LibreCAD first, then FreeCAD, then KiCad, then Blender. Do not skip stages, reorder stages, or recreate the final result in only one software package.
